## Why 005 comes before the deck-builder legality work

The toolchain went in this session (MSVC 19.44, CMake 3.31.6, Qt 6.8.3 `msvc2022_64`, vcpkg SQLite3), and `AGENTS.md`'s evidence table was then run for real.

**All four modules configure and 13 of 13 CTest suites pass** — `client/` 7, `data/` 3, `policy/` 2, `ui/` 1 — on a compiler this code had never been compiled with. That is genuine evidence about the code, independent of CI, and it is not what the brief is about.

Three things nonetheless **fail to build**, none visible to CI because CI is Linux/GCC only:

1. `client/tests/test_protocol_decoder.cpp` — `C4244` narrowing under `/W4 /WX`; `uint32_t` protocol constants into `uint8_t` tuple slots. GCC's `-Wall -Wextra` is silent on it.
2. `data/CMakeLists.txt` — `bench_card_search` forces `/O2`; MSVC rejects that alongside a Debug build's `/RTC1` with `D8016`. A hard error, not a warning, so `/WX` is irrelevant to it.
3. `ui/tests/CMakeLists.txt` — generated QML cache path carries a literal `..` segment Windows cannot `mkdir`. Kills `test_deckbuilder_screen`; `edopro_next_shell` itself builds and links fine.

**Defect 3 blocks the deck-builder legality round**, which touches `ui/` and must produce that suite as evidence.

The brief's most important question is not any of the three fixes: it asks whether the narrowing in (1) also exists in **production** code. Brain only reached the test file — the library linked before the tests compiled. A narrowing conversion in a decoder parsing untrusted `.cdb` and network bytes is a different conversation from one in a test fixture.
